{{Quote|Your Highness, this is a battle I do not think that we can win.|Panaka, to Queen Amidala|<ref name="tpm" />}}
'''Quarsh Panaka''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as the [[Head of Security/Legends|head]] of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] before, during, and after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], and later was the [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] for the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He was a vocal militarist among the peaceful people of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], a fish out of water amongst his peers. Shaken by the murder of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna]], he installed various security measures to make sure that the same thing did not happen to his second monarch, Queen [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. By learning from the mistakes of his predecessor, [[Maris Magneta]], he was able to successfully defend her in several periods of danger, and continued to serve Naboo, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]], and eventually, the Empire.

Notoriously conservative, Panaka often clashed with the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] during the Invasion of Naboo, deriding the Jedi's controversial methods and retaining the utmost faith in his own. Nevertheless, with Jinn's help he was able to get his chance at military action, in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. Panaka thereafter became a staunch supporter of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], rising to the position of Moff of his home [[Sector/Legends|sector]] with Palpatine's patronage.

==Biography==
===Early career===
[[File:Panaka-NEGTC.png|thumb|left|125px|Panaka]]
Quarsh<ref name="EGW cut6">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-6-showdown-at-naboo|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 6: Showdown at Naboo}}</ref> Panaka was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="char" /> around four decades before the beginning of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="birth" /> He was educated offworld in several guilds, specializing in threat analysis and personal combat. Panaka's education was broad, designed to give him the full spectrum of knowledge and training he would need to become an effective security chief.<ref name="char" /> In his education, he traveled to [[Tolan]], and was given instruction from a [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] in the [[Tracker's Guild]].<ref name="mon">{{GamerCite|2|The Monster}}</ref> He later joined a [[Republic Special Task Force/Legends|Republic Special Task Force]] and gained combat experience against pirates. This experience and education served him in good stead upon his return to Naboo and subsequent enlistment in the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]]. While he was off-world, his [[Quarsh Panaka's sister|older sister]] was killed during a training exercise.<ref name="char" />

To deal with this grief, Panaka became increasingly dedicated to his job and to serving the current monarch, [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna]]. He served under [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Maris Magneta]] as a Lieutenant and was paired with [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Bialy]]. He was not known for being sociable&mdash;a character trait he would exhibit throughout his life&mdash;being more focused on being the consummate professional. Panaka was constantly working to improve the security force, and actually invented the liquid-cable grappling hook shooter that became standard amongst his colleagues' weapons.<ref name="char" />

In [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]], Panaka and Bialy were charged with bringing in a [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]], [[Kroke Modbom]], who had apparently been causing trouble in [[Port Landien]]. The pair cornered Modbom at the [[Port Landien Perfumery]], and while Panaka waited to ambush his target in the store's cellar, Bialy went upstairs to confront the Gungan. The lieutenant heard blaster shots ring out, before Modbom burst into the room.<ref name="mon" />

Panaka fought with the Gungan, trying to prevent him from escaping the perfumery. He was successful in subduing the target, although he sustained several injuries to his face in the process. Bialy noted that the Gungan did not have a blaster, and so she supposed that Modbom had an accomplice, who had escaped. Returning to the Palace, Panaka was commended by Magneta, who then introduced him to an aide of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]], [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]]. Pestage was taking Modbom's punishment into Palpatine's hands, much to Panaka's confusion. He mentioned Modbom's supposed accomplice, but Magneta had already assigned the lieutenant to traffic control, as a sea creature had beached itself north of Port Landien.<ref name="mon" />

While blocking off the coastal road near the cove containing the beached creature, Panaka was almost killed when a speeder broke through the roadblock. Calling officers Bialy, [[Pestrak]] and [[Dunni]] on his comlink for backup, Panaka set off in pursuit, chasing the felon to the cove. There, he saw the beached creature for the first time: a legendary [[Sando aqua monster/Legends|sando aqua monster]]. Making his way down into the cove, the lieutenant spotted a white-garbed figure who tried to run him over. Panaka fired off warning shots, but the figure jumped into one of the many nearby rock tunnels. Cautiously, the lieutenant followed, venturing into the pitch black abyss of the Naboo's unmappable rock tunnel network. As he moved further into the tunnels, blindly, he was ambushed by a man codenamed [[Veermok (Naboo)|Veermok]], who was wielding a blaster. Forced to surrender, Panaka was at Veermok's mercy, and was led even deeper into the tunnel network.<ref name="mon" />

Veermok claimed that the tunnels held a stash of secrets that could incriminate King Veruna. He claimed to be fighting for Naboo, and against the lies of its monarchy&mdash;something that Modbom had been doing as well. Panaka was not deterred by the accusations, but before the pair could reach the alleged evidence, the sando aqua monster's movements above caused a cave-in, releasing a torrent of water. Released in the torrent was a wide array of disturbing objects, including eight corpses&mdash;humans and Gungans alike&mdash;and several storage lockers. Panaka was able to reclaim his blaster, and once the commotion was over, Veermok attempted to escape. In response, the lieutenant attempted to shoot him in the back of the knee, but his blaster malfunctioned. Acting quickly, he utilized the liquid grappling cable, and reeled Veermok in. Before he could restrain his captive, Veermok broke free of Panaka's hold, and ran off down the tunnel once more. The lieutenant prepared to utilize his grappling hook again, but before he could, a blaster shot rang out, and Veermok fell to the ground.<ref name="mon" />

The man who had fired the shot was none other than Pestage. Veermok had not perished immediately, but died soon afterward. Panaka was angry at the result, but Pestage, who had intercepted the lieutenant's earlier distress call, pointed out that he had his man. Returning to the palace, Panaka was convinced that Pestage's actions indicated a cover-up of evidence, and that the matter required further attention. He mentioned the bodies, but Magneta claimed that they could have been regurgitated by the monster, or killed by pirates. Nevertheless, Panaka wanted Pestage arrested, but Magneta insisted that everything was being taken care of. Before Panaka could examine the room and its potentially incriminating evidence, Captain Magneta had the area blasted with proton torpedoes from an [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]]. The evidence, which could have pointed at King Veruna or even Senator Palpatine, was destroyed forever.<ref name="mon" />

===Serving Amidala===
[[File:Amidala_SWG5.jpg|thumb|280x280px|Panaka eventually served as head of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces|Royal Security Forces]] of Amidala.]]
[[33 BBY/Legends|Three years later]],<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref><ref name="cod" /> King Veruna abdicated in the wake of a corruption scandal and was killed mysteriously. Magneta failed to prevent this [[Death/Legends|death]] and resigned in disgrace.<ref name="char" /> Panaka was appointed [[Head of Security/Legends|Head of Security]] in Magneta's stead; one of [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala's]] first acts as regent.<ref name="char" /> From his part, Panaka considered the new monarch too young to become Queen. One of her first moves was to dismantle a program established by her predecessor for rebuilding their military forces. As head of the Royal Security Forces,  warned her that she was provoking a harsh [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] response, but she did not listen.<ref name="EGW cut6" /> Panaka took the death of Veruna particularly hard, and he felt the late King's death was his fault.<ref name="char" /> To ensure this never happened again, he developed an elaborate security setup, which involved using the Queen's [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaidens]] as decoys.<ref name="char" /><ref name="DP" /> The ploy saved the life of Amidala more than once.<ref name="char" />

During a [[Coruscant Encounter|diplomatic mission]] to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Panaka and other members of the Royal Naboo Security Forces were fired upon by an [[Darth Maul/Legends|unknown attacker]]. Lieutenant [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]] received permission from Panaka to drive away the attacker.<ref name="SW:BN">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''</ref>

===Invasion of Naboo===
{{Quote|This is a dangerous situation, Your Highness. Our security volunteers will be no match against a battle-hardened Federation army.|Panaka, to Queen Amidala|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:Panaka_Ep1.png|250px|thumb|Panaka shortly before the escape from Naboo|left]]
When the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] blockaded Naboo, Panaka was among the first to recognize the significant threat they posed to the world.<ref name="cswe" /> When they subsequently invaded Naboo, Panaka and his security force were less than well-equipped to defend Theed from them. His forces put up minor resistance, though they surrendered when they fully realized the sheer size of [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9's]] force.<ref name="gb">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> The droids stormed the palace, and took both him and the Queen into custody. Shortly before, Panaka had initiated his decoy scheme, and although the real Queen was captured too, the Neimoidians fell for the ruse, and focused on the [[Sabé/Legends|decoy]].<ref name="tpm" />

As they were being escorted out of Theed, two Jedi Knights, ambassadors that had been sent to resolve the dispute behind the blockade, rescued Panaka, the Queen, the Governor, [[Sio Bibble/Legends|Sio Bibble]], and several security guards. [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], one of the Jedi, wanted to take Amidala to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], against Panaka's initial instincts. The Queen decided against Panaka's judgment, and chose to travel to the capital with the Jedi. Grudgingly, Panaka joined her while Bibble chose to remain behind and look after the Naboo.<ref name="tpm" />

After the Jedi seized the [[Theed Hangar/Legends|Theed Hangar]] from the droids stationed there, the group entered the Queen's [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|personal starship]], and blasted away from Naboo.<ref name="tpm" /> Before he left the planet, Panaka issued an evacuation order to the Royal Naboo Security Forces, ordering them not to engage the enemy except in self-defense.<ref name="SW:BN" /> In trying to get through the blockade, the ship's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] was badly damaged. Jinn's apprentice, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], suggested that they land on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], a desert planet, for repairs. Panaka was outraged at the suggestion, claiming that the Hutts who ruled the planet were gangsters. When Jinn took the suggestion before the Queen, she sided with the Jedi, leaving Panaka in disbelief at her rashness.<ref name="tpm" />

[[File:PaNaKa.jpg|thumb|250px|Panaka aboard the Queen's starship]]
While Jinn, [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], Amidala, and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] went scouting for parts for the hyperdrive, Panaka remained behind and guarded the ship&mdash;ostensibly guarding the Queen. During a sandstorm, the ship received a falsified transmission from Naboo from Governor [[Sio Bibble/Legends|Sio Bibble]], pleading with the Queen to contact him. Kenobi ordered Panaka and the others not to respond, warning it was bait to establish a trace so that the Trade Federation could locate Amidala.<ref name="tpm" />

One night, a band of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] invaded the ship and absconded with the Queen. Panaka asked Kenobi to rescue the Queen from the Tusken Raiders while he stayed on-board to guard the handmaidens. Kenobi successfully defeated the [[Tusken War Chief]] and returned with the Queen.<ref name="SW:OW">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref>

Thanks to the efforts of one [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], Jinn and Amidala had been able to obtain the parts needed to get the ship fully operational again. With the hyperdrive repaired, the group traveled to Coruscant, where they were met by Senator Palpatine. Panaka kept a close eye on Amidala, anticipating an ambush by the Trade Federation, and went with her to the [[Grand Convocation Chamber|Senate Rotunda]] as she and Palpatine put forth their case against the Trade Federation. The Queen's request fell on deaf ears, and she was left with a shaken faith in the Republic. The experience had hardened her resolve, and she decided to return to Naboo, over Panaka's objections, although he tried to explain to her that she would be captured and forced to sign the treaty.<ref name="tpm" />

===Return to Naboo===
{{Quote|I think you can kiss your trade franchise good-bye.|Panaka, to Nute Gunray|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:Panaka_Amidala.png|thumb|left|275px|Panaka protecting Queen Amidala during the Battle of Naboo]]
The Queen had a plan. First, she made contact with [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] and the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Grand Army]] and swayed them to her side. Then she sent Panaka to make contact with the Naboo Security Force on the emergency channel. He met with them on the plains of Naboo atop [[Rasker Hill]] where they were ambushed by a Trade Federation patrol. Fortunately, the [[V-19 landspeeder|Gian speeders]] made short work of the [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platform]]. Panaka made contact with Lieutenant Sykes, who had discovered a Trade Federation convoy. Panaka ordered the pilot to [[Battle of the south ridge|destroy]] the convoy.<ref name="SW:BN" /> He brought back the leaders to plan strategy&mdash;the Gungans would draw the droid army out of the [[City/Legends|city]] and engage in [[Battle of Naboo/Legends#Battle of the Great Grass Plains|battle]]. Meanwhile, the Jedi together with the Naboo would sneak into the palace in [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] and [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|attempt to capture]] [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]].<ref name="tpm" />

[[File:Panaka-Amidala.png|thumb|200px|Panaka and Amidala following the Battle of Naboo]]
Using the secret entrance, Panaka split his forces in two. One group was to distract what droids remained behind while the other, including the Jedi, would liberate the [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] from the Theed Hangar, allowing pilots to disable the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]] [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']] in orbit.<ref name="tpm" /> Panaka directed Sykes as part of the diversionary forces to commence the diversion by firing on an [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tank]].<ref name="SW:BN" /> As Panaka, Amidala and the Jedi set out to find the Viceroy, they were met by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who had been tracking them since their stay on Tatooine. Panaka and Amidala's group were forced to go the long way around while the Jedi stalled the Sith.<ref name="tpm" />

Panaka and Amidala faced heavy resistance as they battled through the streets of Theed to reach the Royal Palace, but they were able to breach the security zone and enter the palace. Once inside the palace, Panaka assisted Amidala in finding the passkeys to unlock blocked portions of the palace.<ref name="SWE1 game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> Progress was frustratingly slow battling through the halls of the Palace, but Panaka came up with an idea. Half the group split off from the main force, clambered out onto a window sill, and used their [[Ascension gun/Legends|ascension guns]] to bypass a level of the Palace. The group made their way through the palace while Sabé led the other half through the main Palace defense force. Unfortunately, Amidala's group were swiftly captured by [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] and escorted to the Viceroy.<ref name="tpm" />

Sabé's group made it to the Throne room and drew out the droids inside while Amidala grabbed a couple of [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] from a secret compartment in the throne, tossed one to Panaka and they eliminated the droids in the room. Defenseless and humiliated, the Viceroy was forced to sign a treaty of surrender.<ref name="tpm" />

After the battle, Nute Gunray and [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]] were handed over by Panaka to the Republic for trial who dryly observed that their time as a successful trade franchise was over.<ref name="tpm" /> During the cleanup, Panaka was challenged to a friendly shooting competition by the Gungan Captain [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]], on account of Panaka's reputation as the quickest shot on Naboo. A target was painted on a disabled Armored Assault Tank. Witnesses said that Panaka won the contest with five bulls-eyes to Tarpals' three.<ref name="char" /> Panaka attended the [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|funeral]] of Jinn, who was killed in the fight with the Sith, before participating in the [[Freedom of Naboo/Legends|celebrations]] following the liberation of Naboo.<ref name="tpm" />

===After the Battle of Naboo===
{{Quote|Actually, I was on my way here to speak with you about security for your return trip to Coruscant.|Panaka, to Senator Amidala|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Panaka.png|thumb|left|180px|Colonel Panaka some time after [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].]]
When Amidala's term as queen of Naboo ended, Panaka remained on Naboo to protect the new Queen, [[Jamillia/Legends|Jamillia]]. Amidala eventually became the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] for the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]]. Although Jamillia was his primary concern, he still looked after Amidala. During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], when [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and his backers seceded from the Republic and formed the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a group of spice miners rallied outside the Palace while Amidala was there. After ensuring that Jamillia was safe, Panaka checked on his former charge. His reason for meeting with her was twofold: He also wanted to make sure she would be safe to return to Coruscant, to vote against the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]]. In a matter of weeks, a security plan was formulated, and Panaka assigned his nephew, Captain [[Gregar Typho/Legends|Gregar Typho]], to protect Amidala. Before she departed for the capital, Panaka informed her that Viceroy Gunray, having escaped punishment, had fallen in with Dooku's Confederacy. Although Typho felt that Amidala, being against the Military Creation Act, would be considered an informal ally of the Confederacy, Panaka was concerned, and cautioned the Senator, as the Confederates had been known to utilize violence against their enemies.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)" />

Some time later, after the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] had broken out, he learned of the marriage between Padmé Amidala and the now-Jedi Anakin Skywalker. Panaka informed Palpatine,<ref name="rotsvd">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> who used this information to his advantage when turning Anakin to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. The ramifications of Panaka's choice would eventually lead to the [[Imperialization/Legends|Imperialization]] of the galaxy,<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> a change that would work to his advantage.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|captainpanaka|Panaka, Captain}}</ref> As Palpatine [[Declaration of a New Order|installed himself]] as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]], Panaka remained extremely loyal to him.<ref name="cswe" />

===Fighting the Skaak Tippers===
{{Quote|As it happens, I'm always in need of good, capable recruits for the Royal Security Force. If you're interested, you can start right away. The Skaak Tippers are brewing up some trouble, and your first assignment would be to find out what.|Colonel Panaka, to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:TTo">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|The Tip-off|Naboo}}</ref>}}
[[File:ColPanaka-TCG.jpg|thumb|200x200px|Colonel Panaka in battle]]
In the early days of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Panaka, now a [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]], was working with the Royal Security Forces in the city of [[Kaadara]] to stop the criminal organization known as the [[Skaak Tippers]] from [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorizing]] the peaceful inhabitants of Naboo. One of Panaka's [[Agent/Legends|agents]], Sergeant [[Willoc]], went missing while investigating a Skaak Tipper plot to steal [[Bank/Legends|bank]] [[Computer/Legends|terminals]] from Kaadara, [[Slicer/Legends|hack]] into them, and gain access to the bank accounts of everyone in the city. Having not heard from Willoc in over a [[Standard week/Legends|week]], Panaka was surprised to receive an unidentified transmission from Willoc's [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]. A [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] investigating an [[old war bunker]] on Naboo discovered the comlink and used it. Panaka urged the spacer to report to him immediately, and seizing the opportunity, enlisted the individual to disrupt the Skaak Tippers' activities in the surrounding area. The spacer obliged, and helped Panaka by wiping out a number of Skaak Tippers, finding one of their radios, and gaining intelligence on a Skaak Tipper [[Confiscation of Skaak Tipper weapons crates|plan]] to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] weapons.<ref name="SWG:TTo" />

Panaka surmised that this was related to the Skaak Tippers' bank heist plot. To discourage the Skaak Tippers from carrying out their crimes, Panaka devised a plan with his newly recruited operative to [[Raid on the Skaak Tipper Hideout|raid]] their nearby [[Skaak Tipper Hideout|Island Hideout]], kill at least sixteen of their members, and [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] their leader, [[Jonni Skaak]], who was actually a former Royal Security Forces agent named Jonthol Mazoon. The assault was a success, and had the effect of crippling the Skaak Tippers' operations. In appreciation for their bravery, Panaka formally inducted his operative as a [[Private/Legends|private]] in the Royal Security Forces, and rewarded the agent with a special Royal Security Forces [[Jacket/Legends|jacket]] and a considerable amount of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="SWG:Ttb">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Tipping the balance|Naboo}}</ref>

===Later service in the Empire===
{{Quote|The Empire has not always lived up to its ideals, Senator Organa – I know that. But it restored order to the galaxy. It snuffed out the fires of Separatism and factionalism. I am proud to have kept Chommell sector safe and secure as part of that effort. Emperor Palpatine saved the galaxy, despite resistance by those you hold dear.|Moff Panaka, to Leia Organa|<ref name="EGW cut6" />}}
Panaka was eventually promoted to [[Commander/Legends|Commander]], and tasked with leading an expedition to the uncharted planet of [[PL-40112-CE-021105]] of the [[Salfrem system]] in [[the Wastes]] region of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. It was during this expedition that he met with [[Bertroff Hissa]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]]-[[Sephi/Legends|Sephi]] hybrid, and also went into a forced alliance with the near humans of the planet to drive off an invasion of interdimensional [[Rozzum]]s. Panaka, alongside Hissa, were the only survivors of the conflict. After returning, Panaka managed to recruit Hissa into the Imperial Military, despite its [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human supremacist]] nature at the time. Panaka even fought for Hissa against his prejudiced peers, up until he himself was promoted to [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the Chommell sector.<ref name="Barely Tolerable 1">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-1|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>

As reward for remaining close to Palpatine during the tumultuous years of the early [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]], Panaka was promoted after the [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|Dissolution of the Imperial Senate]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. As Moff, he represented the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]], replacing [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Pooja Naberrie/Legends|Pooja Naberrie]] in the process.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> To show his continued admiration of Palpatine, Panaka gave him an [[Panaka's gift/Legends|ornate statue]]. The statue was placed in the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] [[Emperor's Throne Room/Legends|receiving chamber]] aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]].<ref name="complete">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> It was destroyed in the station's subsequent destruction at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="rotj">{{Film|VI}}</ref>
[[File:Leia-Zorbathehuttrevenge.jpg|left|thumb|250x250px|Leia Organa (pictured) attempted a peaceful resolution with Moff Panaka, to no avail.]]
Following the death of the Emperor as well as Anakin Skywalker during the Battle of Endor debacle,<ref name="rotj" /> the Galactic Empire shattered, while the Rebellion reorganized itself into a burgeoning [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], Moff Panaka traveled to [[Hosk Station/Legends|Hosk Station]] and met [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], a preeminent figure of the New Republic who he did not realize was the daughter of Queen Amidala whom he once served. Organa, who wished to avoid conflict between her troops and those of the Chommell sector, had arranged that meeting on a neutral site. She attempted to convince the Moff by evoking the memory of the late Amidala, whom he had once served. Panaka did not see any legitimacy in Organa's resurrected Republic, and was not moved by his remembrances of the dead queen. He pointed out that the late Amidala had attracted danger on Naboo and done very little to restore the planet's defenses in the wake of the Trade Federation's invasion. The meeting turned short when Organa told him some members of the Republic were thinking of seizing Naboo, although that threat left Panaka unimpressed.<ref name="EGW cut6" />

By [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], Panaka's fortunes had reversed. The Empire had been defeated and [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|replaced]] by a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. In the new political order, Panaka was replaced with the Gungan senator [[Boma (Gungan)|Boma]] in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]].<ref name="CEIII2">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 2|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 2]]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I'll give them a Panaka blast!|Panaka|<ref name="gb" />}}
[[File:Panaka2-SWE.png|thumb|right|180px|Captain Panaka, [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]]]
Quarsh Panaka was a very pessimistic man and prepared for the worst. During the Naboo crisis, he was clearly annoyed at the fact that Naboo did not have its own planetary army.<ref name="tmpn">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> He often expressed his opinions on this matter, and regularly disagreed with Amidala's Jedi protectors.<ref name="tpm" />

Captain Panaka was often humorless and grim, constantly striving to do the best he could at his job. Panaka was usually on the alert, and was often called "the quickest eyes on Naboo."<ref name="char" /> He possessed keen senses, and was quite intelligent.<ref name="cswe" /> His fellow officers found him distant, demanding, and professional. Panaka took orders, but would voice his opinion when given an order he felt was questionable. One of Panaka's most excited moods occurred when he was successful in protecting his monarch and defeating the Trade Federation.<ref name="tpm" />

Panaka was raised harboring feelings of bigotry towards the Gungans of his homeworld, a view that was common among the Naboo prior to their alliance with the Gungans in the Naboo crisis. This was reinforced by the fact that the Gungans he encountered during his early career were criminals and exiles.<ref name="char" /> Despite this, during the reign of the Galactic Empire, he was willing to allow aliens to serve in the Imperial Military as long as they were extremely capable, as evidenced by his allowing the human-Sephi hybrid [[Bertroff Hissa]] to serve in the Imperial Military.<ref name="Barely Tolerable 1" />

Panaka was bilingual, and could speak [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] in addition to [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].<ref name="son" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I figured the tougher I was, the tougher it would make the Jedi seem to be. Obviously nobody out-toughed the Jedi, but Captain Panaka was going to give them a run for their money!|Hugh Quarshie, on his approach to the role of Panaka|<ref name="SWISouvenir">[[Star Wars Insider Interview Special|''Star Wars Insider'' Interview Special]]</ref>}}
[[File:Panaka-CEUEEd.png|thumb|left|250px|Hugh Quarshie as Captain Quarsh Panaka]]
In [[1999]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], Panaka was played by [[Hugh Quarshie]].<ref name="tpm" /> He was voiced by [[Jeff Coopwood]] in the games [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]],<ref name="SWE1 game" /> ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''<ref name="SW:BN" /> and ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''.<ref name="gb" /> The plot of the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] adaptation of ''The Phantom Menace'' diverges from that of the film, when, shortly after landing on Coruscant, the Queen is assaulted by an assortment of [[Coruscant mercenary|mercenaries]]. The player, as Panaka, fends off the attackers, but the Queen, now isolated from the rest of her entourage, is [[Skirmish at Coruscant|kidnapped]] by more mercenaries, in the employ of a [[Sun Guard]]. Panaka subsequently ventures through Coruscant and saves the kidnapped Queen, killing [[Thug leader|the Sun Guard]] in the process. Panaka then leads the Queen to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] to meet with Palpatine.<ref name="SWE1 game" /><ref name="end">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref>

In the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']], the player, taking the role of the titular Jedi, meets Panaka inside the Theed Royal Palace during an altered scene from the movie. Panaka was fighting the Trade Federation occupation with other soldiers while the Queen was being taken to [[Camp Four/Legends|Camp Four]] by a battle-droid escort. In the movie, Panaka was captured along with the Queen.<ref name="SW:OW" /> This article assumes his presence during the mission is [[Canon|non-canon]].

The character of Panaka was originally intended to appear in [[2002]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], but Quarshie decided not to return, feeling that he wasn't being offered enough money.<ref name="tfn">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/hugh_quarshie_talks_episode_ii_69263.asp|text=Hugh Quarshie talks Episode II|date=2002-01-23|archivedate=20110605101410}}</ref> So, in Panaka's absence, the character of his nephew [[Gregar Typho/Legends|Gregar Typho]] was created.

[[File:LegoEpIStrikeTeam.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Panaka in [[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game|''LEGO Star Wars'']]]]
Panaka was included as a non-player character in the [[2003]] [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> The character was added to the game as part of the [[W:c:swg:Legacy Quest|Legacy Quest]], an expansive series of [[W:c:swg:Quest|quests]] that was released as part of [[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15 2005|Publish 25's]] [[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]] on [[November 15]], [[2005]].<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="NGE">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref> In the game, players could assist Colonel [[W:c:swg:Captain Panaka|Panaka]] by participating in a number of quests to disrupt the [[W:c:swg:Skaak Tipper|Skaak Tippers]]. By completing his final quest, titled [[W:c:swg:Tipping the balance|''Tipping the Balance'']], Panaka would award the player with a [[W:c:swg:RSF|Royal Security Forces]] [[W:c:swg:Jacket|jacket]] and 5901 [[W:c:swg:Imperial Credit|credits]]. Panaka would then reassign the player to Captain [[W:c:swg:Captain Typho|Typho]].<ref name="SWG" /> This eventually presented a continuity error, as Gregor Typho was shown to be killed well before the events of [[W:c:swg:Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies'']] in ''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]'',<ref name="sos">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> a novel released on [[August 26]], [[2008]].<ref name="Penguin">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/139648/street-of-shadows-star-wars-legends-coruscant-nights-book-ii-by-michael-reaves|text=Street of Shadows: Star Wars Legends (Coruscant Nights, Book II)}}</ref>

Panaka was originally slated to appear in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence'']]." He was going to be captured alongside Padmé and be brutally murdered by [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]. He was eventually cut, because at the early stages of production the studio didn't have the ability to include many new characters because of the time it took to create a digital model.<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=threads/29628723|board=Live Action, Clone Wars & Classics|thread=TheForce.Net interviews Henry Gilroy... and Dave Filoni !!! (Your questions answered!)|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207114253/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/theforce-net-interviews-henry-gilroy-and-dave-filoni-your-questions-answered.29628723}}</ref>
